column1: # One line per case and direction, tab-separated:
#   direction  case  behavior  behaviorClose  closeCode  class  note
# behavior    what the suite reports for the case: OK, NON-STRICT, INFORMATIONAL,
#             UNIMPLEMENTED or FAILED; behaviorClose is the same for the closing
# closeCode   the close code the peer saw from this codec (index.json
#             remoteCloseCode; `None` when the connection ended with no code), or `*`
#             for "not compared". A change of 1002 to 1007 is a change of behaviour.
# class       ok             behavior OK and behaviorClose OK: no note.
#             informational  Autobahn only informs here: the case is implementation-defined
#                            or undefined by the spec, so it cannot be OK; the note says what
#                            the codec does and why that is what the RFC requires or allows.
#             non-strict     RFC-permitted but not the strictest reading; note says which.
#             deviation      Autobahn says FAILED and the note says why the codec is right
#                            (never used to excuse a defect: that is a bug to fix).
# A line that is not `ok` needs its sentence; run.py refuses the file otherwise.
# Every case of the suite has a line in both directions (517 each): run.py asks the
# container for the list and fails on a case with no line and on a line with no case.
# `--quick` runs fewer cases and does not change this file.
# Measured against the pinned image (IMAGE), Debian 13 host, loopback, full suite:
#   server direction 779 s, client direction 690 s (about 25 minutes for both);
#   514 OK and 3 INFORMATIONAL in each. The 12.x and 13.x groups (compression) are
#   all but a few seconds of it; see run.py for what --quick leaves out.
# Derived with `run.py --full --propose FILE` and then judged line by line: the
# three INFORMATIONAL cases are the whole of the non-OK set.

column7: Autobahn reports INFORMATIONAL for this case from every implementation that handles it in order: the outcome after a Close is implementation-defined. Here the 256 KiB message is echoed in full, the Close is answered with 1000, and the Ping sent after the Close is not answered (RFC 6455 5.5.1: nothing is processed after a Close), which is what the RFC requires.

Close code 5000 is outside every range RFC 6455 7.4.2 assigns (1000-2999 protocol, 3000-3999 registered, 4000-4999 private) and Autobahn calls the outcome undefined by the spec; the codec refuses it as a protocol error and closes with 1002, which the RFC permits.
